problem: It says that when qⱼ is multiplied by −1, column j of R also changes sign. That is wrong. Since A = QR = Σᵢ qᵢ · (row i of R), the qⱼ term is qⱼ times row j of R, so the sign flip must be applied to row j of R, not to column j. Negating column j of R would change column j of A and break A = QR.
fix: Sign slip: qⱼ can be multiplied by −1, but then row j of R must also change sign (rⱼⱼ becomes negative). A = QR = Σᵢ qᵢ · (row i of R). The usual convention rⱼⱼ > 0 removes the choice. Always check the full product A = QR, not just matching columns of Q on their own.

problem: 'The numbers you subtract are exactly the entries of R' can mislead a student into thinking every entry of R comes from a subtraction. The diagonal entry rⱼⱼ is not subtracted; it is the norm ‖vⱼ‖.
fix: The numbers subtracted at step j are the off-diagonal entries rᵢⱼ = ⟨aⱼ, qᵢ⟩ for i < j. The diagonal entry rⱼⱼ = ‖vⱼ‖ is the length used to normalise, not a number subtracted.

problem: 'At step j only q₁,…,qⱼ₋₁ are used, so entries below row j are zero' is loose. The zeros are in column j, below the diagonal, and the reason needs the span statement.
fix: aⱼ lies in span{q₁,…,qⱼ}, so ⟨aⱼ, qᵢ⟩ = 0 for every i > j. Hence rᵢⱼ = 0 for i > j: column j of R has zeros below the diagonal, so R is upper triangular.
